decision: ocoeco check reads a project's essence as advice and never fails on a gap.
why: A gap is the truth about a project, not an error in its data.
rejected: Failing the check until every step is served.

decision: Hand-work saturation is measured in effort - minutes weighted by load on Borg's CR10 scale - as well as count; there is no deliberate status: looking, listening and deciding are counted and automatable like the rest.
why: The author's 30 kg box: ten seconds, yet draining. And tests must judge sound and pictures themselves, with no person judging mid-run (jidoka).
rejected: Count alone; NASA-TLX's six ratings on every bump (too heavy); exempting judgment from automation.

decision: Hand-work becomes part of ocoeco's language: a handwork table of atomic actions with counts, recorded by ocoeco hand (match, bump, or ask), shown by the observatory as hand-work worth a tool.
why: Proposed by the author. A board task is many steps and never repeats; atomic actions do. The wording is kept from drifting by the tool, as the vocabulary keeps words from drifting.
rejected: Logging whole tasks (they never repeat); free-text notes in the session log (they cannot be counted); bumping on any resemblance without asking (silent merging of different actions).

decision: ocoeco check names every table a repository keeps beside its exported ones but does not export.
why: A device lab's whole backlog and a tool's decisions and log went unseen by the observatory for days; ocoeco note found it by refusing.
rejected: Exporting every file automatically - some are kept for a project's own use.

decision: Hand-work is called manual work everywhere - the table manual_work, the command ocoeco manual, land --manual; every record and bump appends a timed event to manual_events.
why: The author: manual work is the plain word, and with the time kept it can be set beside commits and releases. A command named manual could be read as documentation; the vocabulary defines it, and ocoeco has no documentation command to collide with.
rejected: hand-work (less plain); ocoeco did (the person does, not the tool); inventing times for the history recorded before.

decision: Rows are recorded with ocoeco note, not hand-written per job.
why: Every job wrote its own script to patch JSON: the same handwork again and again, each a chance to break a table. On its first use the tool found that ocoeco itself exported no decisions.
rejected: A per-job script; a general JSON editor that knows nothing of the format.

decision: Research joins the language as its own table (question, found, sources, date); decisions cite it and name the steps they are about; the observatory badges each step with its decisions.
why: Asked by the author: research should back decisions visibly, beside the milestones and progress they concern, and looking around should be a practice for agents and humans alike.
rejected: Sources alone (a list of works says nothing of the question asked); a separate research page with no link to steps.

decision: Vocabulary becomes part of ocoeco's language: a vocabulary table (term, means, not, see), the shared words defined by ocoeco itself, a project's own words beside them, translated like everything else, and shown in views.
why: Asked for by the author, so the work can be spoken about clearly; concepts and vocabulary answer different questions.
rejected: Folding definitions into the concepts table; a glossary written by the observatory about projects.

decision: Where the whole is weakest right now is where attention goes.
why: What should be looked at next, read from every project - not what is loudest.
rejected: triage (medical jargon); focus; priorities (a ranking someone sets)

decision: An idea a project rests on, with why it matters, is a concept.
why: Distinct from idea (why the project exists) and from vocabulary (what a word means).
rejected: principle (a rule to follow, a narrower thing); belief

decision: A shared process that projects call, not copy, is a conveyor.
why: A conveyor carries any load the same way; you put work on it, you do not build your own.
rejected: pipeline (CI jargon, and one run); template (copied, the opposite)

decision: A lens chosen to stand in the observatory's navigation is curated.
why: Says chosen with care, and nothing more; any lens is still found without it.
rejected: featured, pinned (web jargon); official (claims an authority it does not have)

decision: An owned fork pinned upstream and changed only as patches meant to go home is a cutting.
why: Rhizoid's gardening word: a cutting is a living piece of the parent plant, grown in your soil.
rejected: fork (suggests drifting apart); vendored copy (a frozen copy, nothing goes home)

decision: A choice taken, with why and what was rejected, is a decision.
why: The plain word; the rejected options are what make it worth keeping.
rejected: ADR (an acronym a reader must be taught); choice (says nothing of the alternatives)

decision: Minutes weighted by load are effort.
why: Effort is the plain word for time and strain together - the 30 kg box.
rejected: cost (money); toil score (jargon); workload (NASA-TLX's wider measure)

decision: A project's whole chain on one page is its essence.
why: Essence is what a thing most truly is; the page shows why, what, how and now at once.
rejected: overview, summary (say less, not more); dashboard (numbers, no reasons); at a glance

decision: The daily job that writes down what a project's work produced is its gatherer.
why: One metaphor, kept whole: gatherers in each field, the harvest brought in by the observatory.
rejected: collector (monitoring jargon); logger; recorder (plain, but breaks the metaphor)

decision: The observatory's reading of every marked project is the harvest.
why: It brings in what the gatherers gathered; the pair is easy to keep in mind.
rejected: crawl, scrape (say how, not what); sync; import

decision: The three stretches of a path are horizons.
why: Horizons are near and far at once - working, perfection and ongoing perfection are all in view together.
rejected: phase, stage (imply one ends before the next begins); level (sounds like a score)

decision: Why a project exists, told for anyone, is its idea.
why: The everyday word; a reader knows what an idea is without being taught.
rejected: vision, mission (corporate jargon); pitch (selling); purpose (narrower)

decision: A grand view of a family of projects, declared as a small file, is a lens.
why: You look through a lens; many lenses can look at the same commons, and anyone may make one.
rejected: view (every page is a view - two meanings); dashboard; portal

decision: How draining an action was this time is its load.
why: Short and physical, as in carrying a load; one number from Borg's CR10.
rejected: exertion (formal); fatigue (an aftermath, not the act); difficulty

decision: The file by which a repository joins the commons is a mark.
why: Short and plain: a mark is something you put on a thing to say what it belongs to.
rejected: manifest (a package's description elsewhere - two meanings); badge (a picture); tag (GitHub topics are only half of it)

decision: A step on a path is a milestone, reached only when its evidence exists.
why: The word readers know; the vocabulary adds only the rule that evidence reaches it, not a date.
rejected: step (too small to name a stretch of work); goal (aims, not proves); checkpoint

decision: The mirror that reads and draws the commons is the observatory.
why: One watches from an observatory and changes nothing: the mirror, not the control centre.
rejected: dashboard, portal, hub (suggest control)

decision: The commons' language and machinery keep their own name, ocoeco.
why: A proper name, chosen by the author: the observatory's ecosystem - the blood and heart.
rejected: a descriptive name (it is the name of a thing, not a description)

decision: What a project must reach is its path.
why: A path is walked step by step and says nothing of dates - exactly a list of milestones with their evidence.
rejected: roadmap (promises dates, a second meaning we do not want); plan; route

decision: A repository with a mark is a project.
why: The plain word everyone already uses; one repository, one project, one mark.
rejected: repository (says where, not what); module; component

decision: The look around before acting is research.
why: The everyday word for looking into something before deciding.
rejected: prior art (the sources, not the looking); investigation; due diligence (legal)

decision: Manual work done often or heavily enough to ask for a tool is saturated.
why: The author's own word; it says full - nothing more should be carried by hand.
rejected: overdue (blames); hot spot (jargon)

decision: A work a project stands on is a source.
why: The word readers know from any citation.
rejected: reference (also means a pointer); citation (the act, not the work)

decision: The words a project speaks and exactly what they mean are its vocabulary.
why: A vocabulary is a language spoken - the ubiquitous language of domain-driven design - not a list kept at the back.
rejected: glossary (a list at the back of a book); dictionary; terminology (formal)

decision: What actually happens is work: the backlog, the log, what the gatherers record.
why: Plain, and set against the plan; the Essence page asks of it: what is happening now.
rejected: activity (only commits); progress (a judgment, not a record)

decision: How the steps are delivered and proven are its workings, as in the workings of a clock; a single entry is called by its kind.
why: Workings is everyday English for the parts that make something work. Working as a singular noun is unusual and was the weakest word in the language.
rejected: working (unusual as a noun); means (plain, but it would collide with the vocabulary's own means field - one word, two meanings); mechanism (sounds like code only); instrument

decision: Words are chosen like decisions: a vocabulary entry names the decision that chose it, the decision records the words rejected and cites research; every vocabulary is reviewed this way.
why: Asked by the author: wording is part of perfection. A word is how everyone after us will think about the thing.
rejected: Definitions without reasons; leaving the words as they first came.
